title: Quantitative Aspects of Chemical Change

standard_code: Grade 10 Physical Sciences: Quantitative aspects of chemical change
standard_text: The mole and molar mass; calculations with n = m/M and n = N/Nₐ; concentration (c = n/V); percentage composition, empirical and molecular formulae; simple stoichiometric calculations. (summary of CAPS Physical Sciences, Grade 10, Chemistry: Quantitative aspects of chemical change)
meta_desc: Free Grade 10 Physical Sciences worksheets (CAPS): the mole, molar mass, number of particles, concentration, empirical formulae and stoichiometry. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

The mole is the SI unit for amount of substance. One mole of any substance contains 6,02 × 10²³ particles (Avogadro's number). The molar mass M (g·mol⁻¹) is the mass of one mole and is found from the periodic table.

Use n = m/M to change mass to moles, and c = n/V (V in dm³) for solutions. The balanced equation gives the mole ratio of reactants and products. The empirical formula is the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms.

Example

How many moles are in 36 g of water (M = 18 g·mol⁻¹)?

n = m/M

Answer: 2 mol

Example

0,5 mol NaCl in 0,25 dm³. Concentration?

c = n/V

Answer: 2 mol·dm⁻³

Common mistakes

  • Forgetting to change cm³ to dm³.
  • Using the mass ratio instead of the mole ratio.
  • Confusing molar mass with mass.

faq.q: What is the molar mass of CO₂?
What is the difference between an empirical and a molecular formula?
faq.a: The empirical formula gives the simplest ratio (CH₂O); the molecular formula gives the actual numbers of atoms (C₆H₁₂O₆).

items.q: How many particles (molecules or formula units) are in 2 mol of methane (CH<sub>4</sub>)?
How many molecules or formula units are in 1,20 g of H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub>? (N<sub>A</sub> = 6,02 × 10<sup>23</sup> mol⁻¹)
How many particles (molecules or formula units) are in 4 mol of oxygen gas (O<sub>2</sub>)?
How many particles (molecules or formula units) are in 3 mol of aluminium oxide (Al<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>)?
How many moles of atoms in total are in 4 mol of hydrogen chloride (HCl)?
items.e: Each formula has 2 atoms, so 4 × 2 = 8 mol.

items.q: Calculate the mass of 0,050 mol of ZnO.
How many particles (molecules or formula units) are in 1,5 mol of nitrogen gas (N<sub>2</sub>)?
Which reactant is called the limiting reagent?
c: the one that is used up first
items.e: It decides how much product forms.

items.q: How many moles of H atoms are in 0,5 mol of methane (CH<sub>4</sub>)?
items.e: Each formula has 4 H, so 0,5 × 4 = 2 mol.

items.q: How many molecules or formula units are in 8,00 g of HCl? (N<sub>A</sub> = 6,02 × 10<sup>23</sup> mol⁻¹)
How many moles of H atoms are in 2 mol of ammonia (NH<sub>3</sub>)?
items.e: Each formula has 3 H, so 2 × 3 = 6 mol.

items.q: How many particles (molecules or formula units) are in 4 mol of calcium carbonate (CaCO<sub>3</sub>)?
How many molecules or formula units are in 8,00 g of MgO? (N<sub>A</sub> = 6,02 × 10<sup>23</sup> mol⁻¹)
How many particles (molecules or formula units) are in 5 mol of potassium chloride (KCl)?
How many molecules or formula units are in 2,00 g of CH<sub>3</sub>COOH? (N<sub>A</sub> = 6,02 × 10<sup>23</sup> mol⁻¹)
A sample has 3,01 × 10<sup>23</sup> particles of calcium carbonate (CaCO<sub>3</sub>). How many moles is that?
A sample has 1,20 × 10<sup>24</sup> particles of nitrogen gas (N<sub>2</sub>). How many moles is that?
Which is a homogeneous mixture?
items.e: Its composition is the same throughout.

How many particles (molecules or formula units) are in 1,5 mol of sodium carbonate (Na<sub>2</sub>CO<sub>3</sub>)?

How many moles are in 36 g of glucose (C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>12</sub>O<sub>6</sub>)? (Molar mass = 180 g/mol)

How many moles are in 171 g of sucrose (C<sub>12</sub>H<sub>22</sub>O<sub>11</sub>)? (Molar mass = 342 g/mol)
What is the molar mass of potassium chloride (KCl)? (Cl = 35,5, K = 39)
What is the mass of 0,5 mol of carbon dioxide (CO<sub>2</sub>)? (Molar mass = 44 g/mol)
What is the molar mass of magnesium oxide (MgO)? (O = 16, Mg = 24)
What is the mass of 5 mol of potassium chloride (KCl)? (Molar mass = 74,5 g/mol)

How many moles are in 234 g of sodium chloride (NaCl)? (Molar mass = 58,5 g/mol)

How many moles of copper(II) sulfate are in 250 cm³ of a 0,25 mol·dm⁻³ solution?
A solution contains 2,50 mol of ethanol and 3,00 mol of water. What is the mole fraction of ethanol?
How many moles of copper(II) sulfate are in 250 cm³ of a 0,1 mol·dm⁻³ solution?
37,0 g of urea (NH₂CONH₂) is dissolved in water to make 500 mL of solution. What is the molarity? (molar mass 60 g mol⁻¹)
items.e: Moles = 37,0 ÷ 60 = 0,617 mol; M = moles ÷ volume in L = 0,617 ÷ 0,500 = 1,23 mol·dm⁻³.

items.q: 18 g of NaOH is dissolved in 330 g of water. What is the mass percentage of the solute?
items.e: Mass % = mass of solute ÷ mass of solution × 100 = 18 ÷ 348 × 100 = 5,17%.

items.q: A solution of copper(II) sulfate has a concentration of 0,1 mol·dm⁻³. What is its concentration in g/dm³? (Mr = 160)
0,05 mol of sodium chloride is dissolved to make 25 cm³ of solution. What is its concentration?
9,50 g of KCl is dissolved in 500 g of water. What is the molality of the solution? (molar mass 74,5 g mol⁻¹)
items.e: Molality = moles of solute ÷ mass of solvent in kg = 0,128 ÷ 0,500 = 0,255 mol kg⁻¹.

items.q: 1 mol of copper(II) sulfate is dissolved to make 500 cm³ of solution. What is its concentration?
36 g of NaOH is dissolved in 400 g of water. What is the mass percentage of the solute?
items.e: Mass % = mass of solute ÷ mass of solution × 100 = 36 ÷ 436 × 100 = 8,26%.

items.q: 24,0 g of KCl is dissolved in 500 g of water. What is the molality of the solution? (molar mass 74,5 g mol⁻¹)
items.e: Molality = moles of solute ÷ mass of solvent in kg = 0,322 ÷ 0,500 = 0,644 mol kg⁻¹.

items.q: How many moles of sodium hydroxide are in 500 cm³ of a 0,5 mol·dm⁻³ solution?
How many moles of copper(II) sulfate are in 25 cm³ of a 0,1 mol·dm⁻³ solution?
How many moles of hydrochloric acid are in 50 cm³ of a 0,1 mol·dm⁻³ solution?
A solution contains 1,50 mol of ethanol and 6,50 mol of water. What is the mole fraction of ethanol?
13,5 g of H₂SO₄ is dissolved in 100 g of water. What is the molality of the solution? (molar mass 98 g mol⁻¹)
items.e: Molality = moles of solute ÷ mass of solvent in kg = 0,138 ÷ 0,100 = 1,38 mol kg⁻¹.

items.q: A compound has the empirical formula CH<sub>2</sub>O and molar mass = 120. What is its molecular formula?
items.e: M<sub>r</sub> of CH<sub>2</sub>O = 30,0; 120 ÷ 30,0 = 4, so multiply by 4.

items.q: What percent of the mass of sodium chloride (NaCl) is Na? (Na = 23, Cl = 35,5; molar mass = 58,5 g/mol)
What percent of the mass of sodium carbonate (Na<sub>2</sub>CO<sub>3</sub>) is C? (C = 12, O = 16, Na = 23; molar mass = 106 g/mol)
A compound contains 30,4% N, 69,6% O by mass. What is its empirical formula? (Ar: N = 14, O = 16)
items.e: Divide each mass (or %) by Ar, then divide by the smallest number to get the simplest whole-number ratio: NO₂.

items.q: What percent of the mass of sodium hydroxide (NaOH) is O? (H = 1, O = 16, Na = 23; molar mass = 40 g/mol)
What percent of the mass of hydrogen chloride (HCl) is Cl? (H = 1, Cl = 35,5; molar mass = 36,5 g/mol)
A compound contains 46 g of Na, 32 g of S, 64 g of O. What is its empirical formula? (Ar: Na = 23, S = 32, O = 16)
items.e: Divide each mass (or %) by Ar, then divide by the smallest number to get the simplest whole-number ratio: Na₂SO₄.

items.q: A compound contains 16 g of S, 24 g of O. What is its empirical formula? (Ar: S = 32, O = 16)
items.e: Divide each mass (or %) by Ar, then divide by the smallest number to get the simplest whole-number ratio: SO₃.

items.q: What percent of the mass of water (H<sub>2</sub>O) is O? (H = 1, O = 16; molar mass = 18 g/mol)
What percent of the mass of aluminium oxide (Al<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>) is O? (O = 16, Al = 27; molar mass = 102 g/mol)
A compound contains P 43,7%, O 56,3% by mass. What is its empirical formula?
items.e: Divide each % by A<sub>r</sub>, then divide by the smallest: P 1,41, O 3,52.

items.q: What percent of the mass of ethanol (C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>6</sub>O) is C? (H = 1, C = 12, O = 16; molar mass = 46 g/mol)
A compound contains 1,2 g of C, 0,4 g of H. What is its empirical formula? (Ar: C = 12, H = 1)
items.e: Divide each mass (or %) by Ar, then divide by the smallest number to get the simplest whole-number ratio: CH₄.

items.q: A compound contains 88,9% Cu, 11,1% O by mass. What is its empirical formula? (Ar: Cu = 64, O = 16)
items.e: Divide each mass (or %) by Ar, then divide by the smallest number to get the simplest whole-number ratio: Cu₂O.

items.q: What percent of the mass of potassium chloride (KCl) is Cl? (Cl = 35,5, K = 39; molar mass = 74,5 g/mol)
What percent of the mass of methane (CH<sub>4</sub>) is H? (H = 1, C = 12; molar mass = 16 g/mol)
A compound contains 14 g of N, 32 g of O. What is its empirical formula? (Ar: N = 14, O = 16)
items.e: Divide each mass (or %) by Ar, then divide by the smallest number to get the simplest whole-number ratio: NO₂.

items.q: What percent of the mass of iron(III) oxide (Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>) is O? (O = 16, Fe = 56; molar mass = 160 g/mol)
What percent of the mass of carbon dioxide (CO<sub>2</sub>) is C? (C = 12, O = 16; molar mass = 44 g/mol)
A compound contains 85,7% C, 14,3% H by mass. What is its empirical formula? (Ar: C = 12, H = 1)
items.e: Divide each mass (or %) by Ar, then divide by the smallest number to get the simplest whole-number ratio: CH₂.

items.q: When iron rusts: 4Fe + 3O<sub>2</sub> → 2Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>. What is the mole ratio of Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> to Fe?
When aluminium reacts with acid: 2Al + 6HCl → 2AlCl<sub>3</sub> + 3H<sub>2</sub>. What is the mole ratio of H<sub>2</sub> to HCl?

When sulfur dioxide is oxidised: 2SO<sub>2</sub> + O<sub>2</sub> → 2SO<sub>3</sub>. What mass of SO<sub>2</sub> react with 128 g of O<sub>2</sub>? (O<sub>2</sub> = 32 g/mol, SO<sub>2</sub> = 64 g/mol)
When iron rusts: 4Fe + 3O<sub>2</sub> → 2Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>. What mass of O<sub>2</sub> react with 28 g of Fe? (Fe = 56 g/mol, O<sub>2</sub> = 32 g/mol)
When iron is made in a blast furnace: Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO<sub>2</sub>. What is the mole ratio of Fe to CO<sub>2</sub>?

When ammonia is made from nitrogen and hydrogen: N<sub>2</sub> + 3H<sub>2</sub> → 2NH<sub>3</sub>. What mass of N<sub>2</sub> is needed to make 8,5 g of NH<sub>3</sub>? (NH<sub>3</sub> = 17 g/mol, N<sub>2</sub> = 28 g/mol)
When potassium chlorate decomposes: 2KClO<sub>3</sub> → 2KCl + 3O<sub>2</sub>. What mass of O<sub>2</sub> form along with 149 g of KCl? (KCl = 74,5 g/mol, O<sub>2</sub> = 32 g/mol)

When glucose is used in respiration: C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>12</sub>O<sub>6</sub> + 6O<sub>2</sub> → 6CO<sub>2</sub> + 6H<sub>2</sub>O. What mass of H<sub>2</sub>O form from 720 g of C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>12</sub>O<sub>6</sub>? (C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>12</sub>O<sub>6</sub> = 180 g/mol, H<sub>2</sub>O = 18 g/mol)
When iron rusts: 4Fe + 3O<sub>2</sub> → 2Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>. What mass of Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> form from 168 g of Fe? (Fe = 56 g/mol, Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> = 160 g/mol)
When propane burns in a grill: C<sub>3</sub>H<sub>8</sub> + 5O<sub>2</sub> → 3CO<sub>2</sub> + 4H<sub>2</sub>O. What is the mole ratio of C<sub>3</sub>H<sub>8</sub> to CO<sub>2</sub>?
When iron rusts: 4Fe + 3O<sub>2</sub> → 2Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>. What mass of Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> form from 14 g of Fe? (Fe = 56 g/mol, Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> = 160 g/mol)
When iron is made in a blast furnace: Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO<sub>2</sub>. What is the mole ratio of CO<sub>2</sub> to Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>?
When sodium reacts with chlorine: 2Na + Cl<sub>2</sub> → 2NaCl. What is the mole ratio of Cl<sub>2</sub> to NaCl?
When propane burns in a grill: C<sub>3</sub>H<sub>8</sub> + 5O<sub>2</sub> → 3CO<sub>2</sub> + 4H<sub>2</sub>O. What is the mole ratio of O<sub>2</sub> to CO<sub>2</sub>?
When aluminium reacts with oxygen: 4Al + 3O<sub>2</sub> → 2Al<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>. How many moles of O<sub>2</sub> react with 2 mol of Al?
items.e: 2 mol Al × (3 mol O<sub>2</sub> ÷ 4 mol Al) = 1,5 mol.

items.q: When sulfur dioxide is oxidised: 2SO<sub>2</sub> + O<sub>2</sub> → 2SO<sub>3</sub>. What is the mole ratio of O<sub>2</sub> to SO<sub>3</sub>?
When propane burns in a grill: C<sub>3</sub>H<sub>8</sub> + 5O<sub>2</sub> → 3CO<sub>2</sub> + 4H<sub>2</sub>O. What is the mole ratio of CO<sub>2</sub> to H<sub>2</sub>O?
When iron is made in a blast furnace: Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO<sub>2</sub>. What is the mole ratio of CO to Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>?
When hydrogen burns in oxygen: 2H<sub>2</sub> + O<sub>2</sub> → 2H<sub>2</sub>O. What is the mole ratio of H<sub>2</sub>O to O<sub>2</sub>?
When propane burns in a grill: C<sub>3</sub>H<sub>8</sub> + 5O<sub>2</sub> → 3CO<sub>2</sub> + 4H<sub>2</sub>O. How many moles of O<sub>2</sub> are needed to make 6 mol of CO<sub>2</sub>?
items.e: 6 mol CO<sub>2</sub> × (5 mol O<sub>2</sub> ÷ 3 mol CO<sub>2</sub>) = 10 mol.
